name: Iceburn
label: Revelation
lede: Salt Lake City straight edge kids who covered Miles Davis on a hardcore label, grew into a seven-piece free jazz collective, vanished for two decades, and came back with two songs that fill an entire LP.

eras.title: Out of the Salt Lake straight edge scene
eras.text: Gentry Densley came up through Salt Lake City hardcore bands (Brainstorm, Better Way, Headstrong, then Insight) before starting Iceburn as a power trio. The first record went to Victory, a deal Densley came to regret.

years.h: Gentry Densley starts Iceburn in Salt Lake City
years.p: Guitarist and singer Gentry Densley, drummer Joseph "Chubba" Smith and guitarist James Holder form Iceburn, partly out of the Salt Lake straight edge band Insight.

q: We always felt we were getting ripped off, from the beginning.
years.src: Veil of Sound · Echoes and Dust
years.p: Iceburn go to Victory because Insight had worked with the label. Gentry Densley says the band felt ripped off from the start and later hired a lawyer to get its rights back.

years.h: Revelation's Jordan Cooper signs Iceburn after hearing Firon
years.p: Iceburn are outsiders to Revelation's youth crew roster, but label head Jordan Cooper signs them on the strength of Firon and backs them through every change that follows.

eras.title: Four sides, four songs, pay phones
eras.text: On Revelation, Iceburn stretched out: a double album with one song per side, a sax player, two Miles Davis covers. They crossed the country with Engine Kid on folding maps and pay phones and played some of the strangest shows of their lives.

years.src: Discogs · Revelation Records pressing history · Wikipedia
years.h: Hephaestus: a double LP with one song per side · REV 27
years.p: Four sides, four tracks: Iron, Brick, Flyswatter and Blacksmith. Gentry Densley, bassist Cache Tolman and drummer Joseph Smith, recorded at Fast Forward Studios with Tony Korologos.
years.xp: Revelation pressed 1,010 on black and 305 on white. Most of Iceburn's artwork came from California artist [[Rich Jacobs|8b6fa77a-43b6-43a4-bc21-09b3015a590a]].

years.h: Iceburn record Poetry of Fire with a tenor sax
years.p: Iceburn cut Poetry of Fire with Greg Nielsen on tenor saxophone and James Holder back on second guitar, the first step toward a jazz band.

years.h: Live at the Endzone, Kingston PA, September 3, 1993
yt: Live at the Endzone, Kingston PA, September 3, 1993

years.src: Echoes and Dust · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Iceburn and Engine Kid tour on pay phones and folding maps
years.p: Iceburn cross the US again and again with [[Engine Kid|899baef6-af48-4caa-aff6-c1562a5dc12d]], [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]]'s band, and share a split 12" on Revelation. One night they open for guitarist [[Caspar Brötzmann|34b6582f-e04b-453e-800f-550fc62ba5b8]], a show Gentry Densley calls life affirming.
years.xp:
Densley remembers the tours as no cell phones, no internet, just pay phones and big folding maps. The Iceburn/Engine Kid split (REV 34) was pressed 1,363 on black and 200 on salmon.

They also played regularly with [[Lungfish|5af88bca-9c13-424a-b63c-b5c96c69cb0e]], and toured with a reunited [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]], [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]]'s band before [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]], as a benefit for the Western Shoshone.

years.h: Bullwhips and leg wrestling at an Iceburn show in Olympia
years.p: An Iceburn show in Olympia, Washington, with Suckdog and Hazel involves bullwhips and Indian leg wrestling, and ends with ambulances, as Gentry Densley tells it.

years.h: Poetry of Fire covers Miles Davis · REV 36
years.p: Two Miles Davis tunes, Stones (from Milestones) and Blues (from All Blues), sit beside the sixteen-minute Poem of Fire. The CD runs 72 minutes; the vinyl cuts the covers.

eras.title: The Iceburn Collective
eras.text: Iceburn changed its name to admit what it had become: a rotating group of up to seven players with saxophone, congas and a second guitar. Each record leaned further toward improvisation until, by the last one, nothing was written down at all.

years.h: Meditavolutions and a new name: the Iceburn Collective
years.p: Seventy minutes on two LPs (REV 49), with Gentry Densley adding sitar and the twenty-two-minute Sphinx at its center. Recorded in December 1994, it comes out under the name the Iceburn Collective.
years.xp: The line-up: Densley, James Holder on guitar, Greg Nielsen on tenor sax, Daniel Day on drums and Doug Wright, back on bass, with Randy Herbert on percussion. Critic Bret Love wrote that it may take a few songs to realize you've never heard anything like this Utah septet.

years.h: Polar Bear Suite: Iceburn start their own label
years.p: The Iceburn Collective release Polar Bear Suite through their own Iceburn Records, with Revelation. Power of the Lion follows in 1998.

years.src: Echoes and Dust · Veil of Sound
years.h: The Iceburn Collective play Stravinsky's Rite of Spring live
years.p: Among the stranger nights of the collective era: an Iceburn arrangement of Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring, played on stage. Guitarist [[Ed Rodriguez|b88667bb-99ae-4635-a2a3-d311d59e2b8b]], later of [[Deerhoof|11eabe0c-2638-4808-92f9-1dbd9c453429]], passes through the band in these years.

years.h: Land of Wind and Ghosts: Iceburn go fully improvised
years.p: The last Iceburn record of the era comes out on Mountain Collective Records. By now, Wikipedia says, the group is an entirely improvised avant-garde jazz ensemble built around saxophones and woodwinds.
years.xp: It followed Speed of Light Voice of Thunder (1999) on Iceburn Records. Soon after, the collective stopped.

eras.title: SLUG throws a party
eras.text: Gentry Densley moved into doom and drone with Greg Anderson in Ascend and his own Eagle Twin. Iceburn itself came back for one night for the Salt Lake magazine that had championed it all along, and the old players quietly kept meeting after that.

years.h: Iceburn reunite for SLUG Magazine's 18th birthday
years.p: Salt Lake City's SLUG Magazine, a steady supporter of Iceburn and Gentry Densley, gets a one-night Iceburn reunion. Densley, Joseph Smith, James Holder and Cache Tolman keep playing together after it.

Densley starts [[Eagle Twin|d6778ca0-914b-4c84-9754-c2c9e4b49154]], which debuts on Southern Lord in 2009. He has also teamed with [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]] of [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]] in the doom project Ascend.

years.h: Southern Lord reissues Iceburn's Power of the Lion on vinyl
years.p: Greg Anderson's Southern Lord puts Iceburn's 1998 Power of the Lion out on vinyl, the start of the label's link with the band.

eras.title: The firebird rises
eras.text: Twenty-one years after their last record, Iceburn put out new music on Southern Lord: two long pieces by the 1990s core of Gentry Densley, Joseph Smith, James Holder and Cache Tolman, all of them fathers now.

years.src: The Obelisk · Echoes and Dust · Veil of Sound
years.h: Asclepius: Iceburn's first album in over twenty years
years.p: Two tracks, Healing the Ouroboros and Dahlia Rides the Firebird, recorded by Andy Patterson and released on Southern Lord.
years.xp: The band recorded four songs before the pandemic and chose two to fit an LP. Gentry Densley said the images of the firebird and the ouroboros felt right for a return after so long.
